content.summary: Accept this exact version as ready for the separate final audits. The two clarifications are supported, and the targeted cap15 dependency check reveals no circular use. No necessary revision remains from my review. This round does not grant final publication approval or claim a complete independent replay; external theorem imports and software-assurance limits remain material.

findings.statement: New metadata identifies the reconstructed root as the named commit’s tree; it does not authenticate the historical H27 execution.
findings.disposition: The revised paragraph accurately distinguishes the original inconsistent response, the later identifier relationship, and the separate historical-run limitation.

revisions.action: Rechecked the actual-member maximum definition, N43 anchor and graph-degree identities on final bytes.
revisions.result: The required universal quantifier remains explicit and correct.

revisions.action: Compared the new primary response fields with a fresh hash of the preserved root payload.
revisions.result: The identifier relationship is now supported; the original response inconsistency and historical-run boundary remain qualified.

checks.scope: H27 identifier clarification and permissible assurance inference.
checks.method: Parsed the preserved h27-commit-response.json and independently hashed the 266-byte retained payload using the Git tree header.
checks.observation: Metadata names commit d4d5723267c662291efdadfa6e7061d919e76fa9 and tree 0a3e3838650fc981133940e798c9d220140e785e; the latter exactly matches the independent rehash. The response also records deletion of the archive-hash command, consistent with the retained README/script distinction. None of this proves why the earlier response used the wrong identifier, verifies the archived search, or establishes source-to-run authentication. Section 2 makes only the supported relationship claim.

checks.scope: Neighbourhood quantifiers, fixed cardinality and global reduction.
checks.method: Re-derived the graph identities and compared Sections 3–6 and the revised conclusion with GLOBAL67-ordinary-theorem.md.
checks.observation: For each actual R, its disjoint family is intersecting, so H27 gives |N[R]|>=68-27=41. Hence mu>=41, not equality. Separately delta(G)=68-N[max], giving 24 at N[max]<=44 and 25 at N[max]<=43. The proof first restricts to the same 68-member family and does not inherit minimum used degree through deletion. Degree cases 20,19,18,17,16 and at most15 exhaust the universal cap20; guarded cap18 imports activate only after D19. The conclusion’s revised inequality introduces no premise.

checks.scope: Cap15 prerequisite versus later rho exclusions and objection readiness.
checks.method: Read LOW15-NO44-ordinary-closure.md and the cap15 assembly; independently constructed all literal R16 one-deletions and all P8 intersection-two deletions, then compared retained guards with committed objections.
checks.observation: All 240 surviving R16-minus-one triples avoid degree patterns (2,4,4) and (3,3,4). All 120 tested P8 members and eight Q8 members have a degree-five point. These support the stated N44 obstruction after its separately proved exact-rho7 reduction; it does not borrow the later rho<=6 theorem. Final text retains maximum-degree root selection, rho<=6 support restriction, separate rho8 gluings, B4 guards and proper-trace multiplicities. The 13 historical required revisions have recorded original-reviewer resolutions. Source hashes and bounded results are preserved in checks/round10/alpha/; no heavy suite was rerun.
